transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I’m… I’m having a hard time keeping up at work. I’ll sit there staring at one audit workpaper for like twenty minutes before I can even make myself move my hand to type. People have started noticing.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?
Yeah… most days. I wake up and it’s just this… heavy, empty feeling in my chest. Like the day’s already ruined before I even get out of bed.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like?

Not really. I used to be the kind of person who’d plan hikes, take pictures, cook on Sundays… volunteer at the library sometimes. Now it all just feels like… tasks on a list I don’t care enough to even start.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge lately?
I don’t know… maybe a little. I’m mostly just tired and kind of tense, I guess. Hard to tell.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About seven months, I guess. It kind of started after my husband stopped working… after the downsizing.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?
Not really. I mean… hiking, taking photos, cooking, the library volunteering—those used to be nice. Now they just feel like things I’m supposed to do, and I can’t really bring myself to start.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight recently?
Yeah… a bit. I haven’t really been eating much unless I make myself, and some of my work skirts are looser. I’m not trying to lose weight or anything.
Do you feel like you're moving more slowly than you used to?

Yeah. I think so. I’m just… slower. At work I can sit there staring at the same audit workpaper for twenty minutes before I even get my hand to type anything. People have started noticing I’m not keeping up.
Have you had any thoughts of not wanting to live or wishing you were dead?
I… I don’t really know how to answer that. I don’t think I want to talk about it much.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself?
I… I don’t know. I’d rather not get into that right now.
How often do you feel like you're unable to experience any pleasure at all?

Most of the time, I guess. I used to make plans to hike, take photos, cook on Sundays, volunteer at the library… now it all just feels like a list of things I’m supposed to do, and I can’t really make myself care enough to start.
Do you feel like these feelings of sadness and emptiness are interfering with your daily life most of the time?

Yeah… most of the time. Work’s been harder. I’ve missed review deadlines, and I’ve had to pass off parts of audits I’d normally handle myself.

At home, my husband’s been doing the bills and insurance forms because I just… can’t reliably get through them.
Do you feel like you're moving slower physically, not just taking longer to start tasks?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not just getting started. I’ll sit there at work staring at one audit workpaper for… I don’t know, twenty minutes, and even moving my hand to type feels slow. People have noticed I’m not keeping up.
Do you feel like these feelings of sadness and emptiness are present nearly every day?
Yeah… pretty much nearly every day. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling, like the day’s already ruined before I even get up.
Do you feel like these feelings of sadness and emptiness are worse in the morning?
Yeah… mornings are usually the worst. I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day’s already kind of lost before I’m even out of bed.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience any pleasure at all most of the time?
Yeah… most of the time. I used to do things like plan hikes, take photos, cook on Sundays, volunteer at the library. Now it all just feels like… stuff on a list. I don’t really care enough to start.
Do you feel like you're resting or sleeping more than usual?
I’m not really sure. I’m tired a lot, but I don’t know if I’m actually sleeping more… I haven’t been keeping track.
Do you feel like you're physically slowing down, like your body is moving more slowly than it used to?

Yeah. I think so. I’ll just… sit there at my desk, staring at one audit workpaper for ages, like twenty minutes, before I even make myself type anything. People at work have noticed I’m not keeping up.
Have you had a period of at least two weeks where you felt better, with less sadness and more energy, since these symptoms started seven months ago?
I don’t know… not really that I can remember. Maybe a day here or there felt a little less bad, but I can’t think of two weeks where I actually felt better.
Do you feel like your symptoms are severely impairing your ability to function in daily life?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still getting by, but not like before. At work I’ve missed review deadlines, and I’ve had to hand off parts of audits I usually handle myself. And at home my husband’s been doing the bills and insurance stuff because I just… don’t get through it reliably.
